topic: Half your oxygen comes from the ocean
claim: About half of Earth's oxygen production comes from the ocean, mostly from tiny drifting plankton; one bacterium, Prochlorococcus, makes up to 20% of the biosphere's oxygen.

beats.caption: HALF OF EARTH'S OXYGEN
beats.vo: Half of Earth's oxygen comes from the ocean.

beats.caption: BUT NOT FROM SEAWEED
beats.vo: Not from whales, not from seaweed. From plankton, drifting plants and algae too small to see.

beats.caption: PHOTOSYNTHESIS, AT SEA
beats.vo: Just like leaves, they soak up sunlight and carbon dioxide, and release oxygen. And blooms of them are so big, satellites can see them from space.

beats.caption: PROCHLOROCOCCUS
beats.vo: One bacterium, Prochlorococcus, the smallest photosynthesizer on Earth, makes up to twenty percent of the oxygen in our whole biosphere.

beats.caption: THE CATCH
beats.vo: The catch: marine life uses up about as much oxygen as the ocean makes. Most of the air you breathe was stored in the atmosphere over hundreds of millions of years.

beats.caption: PROTECT THE PLANKTON
beats.vo: So the ocean doesn't just touch your breath. It helped build the air you breathe.

sources.text: NOAA National Ocean Service, How much oxygen comes from the ocean? https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/ocean-oxygen.html
